# Context from my IDE setup:

## Active file: tacto-negotiator/docs/v2/implementation-order-addendum-2026-10-10.md

## Active selection of the file:
# V2 capability delivery: approved implementation-order addendum

**Approved by the user:** checkpoints A and B progress together wherever dependencies allow.
Sections A–F retain the original assessment/proposal snapshot below; sections G–M record the
subsequent implementation (evidence-to-economics integration in K, the used-action boundary in L,
and typed assembly/offline coordination in M). No complete loop, persistence system, or whole DTO inventory is
required before independently implementing/testing interpretation, economics, or strategy.

10 October 2026. Assessment of checkout `a88bf86` **including the existing working-tree
planning/test changes**. This is a proposal, not an approved contract revision or a completion
claim. No production code, tests, fixtures, or existing planning documents were changed for
this assessment. Task IDs, architecture, and C's implemented-type contracts remain authoritative.

The smallest useful adjustment is to **implement contracts beside their first consumers,
and bring real evidence resolution, economics, validation, and behavioral evaluation forward**.
Do not wait for all D1–D16 to start component work. Do not promise that the complete existing
pipeline can use only a handful of DTOs: its current public input and result types have a
substantial transitive dependency closure.

## A. Actual state and architectural assessment

| Area | Inspected implementation state | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| T1.1a | Frozen values/terms, strict parsing, canonical serialization/hashes, errors implemented | Reuse unchanged |
| T1.1b | Assessment models and exact Protocol declarations implemented | Reuse; declarations referencing absent DTOs do not make the ports executable end to end |
| T1.1c | DecisionStage/DecisionRecord/EffectiveConfig and config resolver implemented | T1.3 composition and T1.4 record persistence remain unfinished |
| T1.1d | EvidenceScope, Provenance, TemporalValidity, DisclosureRule implemented | All 160 remaining declared exports are absent: 146 concrete DTOs plus 14 unions |
| T1.2a/b | No recorded adapter, factory, or orchestration loop | Normalizer, scripted fakes, and sentinel routing test are preparation |
| T2–T6 | No concrete V2 evidence, interpreter, economics, strategy, execution, store, or evaluation components | Planned tests and V1 implementations are reuse material, not delivered V2 capabilities |
| V1 | Existing negotiator, arithmetic integrations, adviser, evidence, runtime, Lab infrastructure | Preserve named historical baseline; wrap useful primitives rather than assume current callers are safe |

Fresh local verification in this pass:

- `tests/v2`: **380 passed, 796 xfailed**, no unexpected failures. Many passes validate
  specification examples; the 796 explicit missing-component/DTO xfails are not completed work.
- Ruff over `src/negotiator/v2 tests/v2`: passes.
- Frozen V1 replay: exact historical first move matches `3653046`; no network/model calls.
- Six focused legacy modules from A's verification recipe: **56 passed, 4 failed**.
  Failures remain the inverse-price regression, two final-offer history/memory expectations,
  and empty-thread mocked-agent compatibility (`test_evaluator.py` and `test_context.py`).
  This is a bounded check, not a full repository readiness claim.

Preserve evidence / interpretation / strategy / economics / validation / execution /
orchestration boundaries, dependency injection, strict contracts, deterministic finances,
independent validation, source applicability/provenance, reproducible records, and the pinned
official kit. Keep the existing serial coordinator and SQLite direction. Preserve V1 goldens
and audit obligations in A §4. The source inspected still contains the legacy inverse helper,
separate cost access, and mutable runtime paths; none becomes safe through this proposal.

The avoidable dependencies are **whole-task barriers**: T1.2a, T1.4, T2.1, and T4.1 name
all of T1.1d; the instructions require the exact serial D1–D16 order; T6.1 waits for M5.
T5.1 also waits for all of T2.3 even for an offer with no factual claims. These are broader
than their first consumers need. Preserve real prerequisites: constructors need their field
types and complete union members; economic joins need verified basis/standards; grounding needs
actual source/message references; sending needs validation and durable ownership.

## B. Minimal roadmap delta and critical path

Keep M0–M7 and T identifiers. A–E below are **capability checkpoints across existing tasks**,
not replacement milestone IDs. A partial parent remains in progress until all its original
acceptance criteria pass. Keep shared-model edits serial; a new component may follow each
dependency-complete contract handoff rather than waiting for all batches.

| Checkpoint | Required work and order using existing IDs | Exit gate / status |
|---|---|---|
| A: functional backbone | T1.1d types on demand; T1.2a P10 binding; T1.3 offline composition; T1.4 artifact/record append/reload; T1.2b complete typed loop. Bring T4.1 official package evaluation and the used offer/question subset of T5.1 forward. Context, interpretation, strategy, generation and feedback may initially be recorded ports | Actual ten-stage loop, deterministic costs, independent used-action checks, fake execution and feedback, saved/reloaded trace. **Required next, not implemented; scripted intelligence explicitly labelled** |
| B: evidence-driven intelligence | Start T2.1 now; replace A's mock context with resolver-backed context. T3.1 labels + T6.1 local behavioral controls start now. Add T3.2 bounded deterministic interpretation/fallback and grounded draft validation, T4.2 finite generation, T4.3 evidence-conditioned proposal and deterministic selector. Add needed T2.3 standards/estimate projections; add T2.2 preparation when reading real package data | Relevant evidence/reply changes alter defensible intent and, when affordable/legal, selected action; irrelevant wording does not. Actual interpretation/strategy algorithms, evaluator and validator run. **Required next after/alongside backbone** |
| C: reliable execution | Complete used-scope T2.2/2.3 and T5.1; T5.2 projector + atomic state/operation/claim transaction; T5.3 endpoint gateway/executor/recovery; T5.4 serial multi-turn loop and basic feedback. Add minimum T3.3 budget plumbing if using a model. T6.2 only for the intended CLI/Lab launch path | Local simulator plus crash/uncertain-outcome/restart gates before any real execution. Live readiness remains separate from local proof and needs operational authorization. **Required later** |
| D: experimental framework | Register baseline and evidence-conditioned bundles through existing T1.3/T4.3 seams; extend T6.1 to identical recorded situations. Add T4.4 bounded LLM selector and T3.3/3.4 interpretation/provider evaluations when chosen and funded; T6.3/6.4 retain performance/promotion gates | Same evidence/economic/validation services, distinct strategy/config identities, held-out reports. Basic substitutability checked already in A/B. **Required later; model selector optional** |
| E: advanced capabilities | Retain T2.4 broader documents, T4.5 generic solver, T7.1–7.5 category/information-value/async/research/basket expansion and F's research queue. Sophisticated memory, preference estimation and attribution algorithms remain here | Enable on concrete requirement or measured gap. **Deferred; optional experiments remain optional** |

Shortest credible paths, with no full-parent completion hidden in these arrows:

1. **Offline loop:** dependency-complete T1.1d groups → P10-only T1.2a → T1.3
   composition + T1.4 append/load → T1.2b with real T4.1 and a real T5.1 used-action
   subset → checkpoint A. Storage is append-only decision/artifact storage at this stage;
   do not require the full live StateStore implementation to replay a decision.
2. **Evidence-sensitive decision:** T2.1 resolver/context + T3.1/T6.1 controls → T3.2
   bounded real interpretation → T4.2/T4.3 + necessary T2.3 projections → run through A's
   economic/validation pipeline → checkpoint B. The first bounded interpreter may safely
   recognize structured offers and explicit supported signals, preserving exact citations and
   unknowns. It must derive outputs from current inputs, not select prewritten assessments by
   fixture ID. Broader language coverage uses the same port and later evaluated model adapter.
3. **Reliable real execution:** B + strict data preflight/relationship estimates → full
   used-scope T5.1 → T5.2 → T5.3 → T5.4, intended launch-path checks and runtime fault matrix
   → checkpoint C. No model is required for a deterministic baseline. If enabled, its absolute
   budget/cancellation/fallback gates are prerequisites to transmitting.

Do not let A become another long framework project. Replace each scripted decision component
as its types become available; use T2.1 and T4.1 direct component demonstrations before A is
complete. Basic feedback is observed linkage, not learned causal attribution. Persist operation
identity/provenance before real sending; an unknown outcome retains its original ID/bytes and
blocks a conflicting action. All closing paths still need fresh standing-sheet checks and the
same deterministic close evaluator. Supplier prose never establishes terminal truth.

## C. DTO classification and limits of deferral

The existing layout can stay. Public cross-module contracts include evidence/context,
assessment, intent/candidate/evaluation/decision, validated action, operation, and result
envelopes. Nested contract helpers such as term origins and cost components also remain
explicit. Provider projection DTOs belong at the adapter boundary; hydrated events belong at
the store/projector boundary. They are not all necessary to *algorithm development*, but
their present contract placement is not a reason to migrate packages.

Private ranking scores, search queues, parser working structures, caches, and strategy-specific
reasoning can remain internal typed models. Do not add them to core speculatively. Existing
StrategyMemory supports owned payload schemas by reference; defer its algorithm, not its
referenced shape if NegotiationState already requires it. Empty tuples or disabled estimates
do not remove the need to define the complete declared type/union.

Static closure check: start with PreparedEvidence, DecisionSnapshot, IntentBatch,
GenerationResult, EvaluationBatch, NegotiationDecision, RenderedAction, ValidationResult,
PendingOperation, DispatchPermit, TransportBudget, ExecutionResult, EventProposal, ReplayResult,
VerifiedClaim and OfficialCostResult. Recursively follow field type names and every union member
in `tests/v2/dto-contracts.json`. This reaches **128 of 160 remaining exports** (DTOs and
unions), before any model/gateway envelopes. Adding ModelRequest, ModelBudget, ModelResult,
GatewayResult and ServerObservation for the existing integration seams reaches **148 of 160**.
These are schema dependency counts, not proof that a codec/test cutline needs exactly that
many; full port introspection and optional scenario bindings may require more. Record the
chosen consumer roots and exact symbol set before assigning each integration handoff.

| Batch | First-loop classification under the existing model/gateway seams | Safety / later / optional distinction |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | All 8 fact payloads via EvidencePayload | Preserve closed union even if first fixture only uses CostFact/TextRecord |
| D2 | 11/12 including evidence records, preparation, conflicts, context | ResolvedCostInput joins needed with T2.3; integrity/applicability never deferred when consuming evidence |
| D3 | All 13 case/buyer/terms/alternative exports | Essential correctness; unavailable alternative cannot become zero/infinity |
| D4 | All 11 economics/policy/evaluation exports | Essential economics. Scenario shapes required; scenario estimation/robust algorithms can follow. Live relationship-sensitive use needs estimates or documented admitted degraded scope |
| D5 | All 11 intent/candidate/batch/decision exports | Stable strategy/economic boundary, including complete CandidateContents union |
| D6 | All 10 message/server/clock/round/terminal exports | Essential input shapes. Authoritative terminal, deadline and round proof is live safety, not permission to infer it offline |
| D7 | 7/11: ClaimWindow, VerifiedClaim and closing result shapes | ClaimCandidate/results/verification union needed when enabling factual claims and full T5.1; closing shapes arrive through ReplayResult even before close algorithms |
| D8–D9 | All rendering, validation, budgets, operation and permit exports | Essential used-action boundary; durable commit/permit issuance is checkpoint C behavior |
| D10–D11 | All state/context/outcome exports | Required by existing signatures; advanced memory/attribution behavior deferred despite available schemas |
| D12–D13 | 10/11 each for existing model/gateway seams | DocumentBytes later with document fetch; SelectorResponse optional T4.4. Without those gateway seams, both groups can follow the first mock-port loop, but existing model-variability acceptance remains outstanding |
| D14 | All 8 via EventPayload | Shapes required by FeedbackProcessor's EventProposal; event-store transitions completed at C |
| D15 | 9/14 via EventProposal/EventPayload | NegotiationEvent, DecisionCommit, CommittedResult, ConflictResult, CommitResult required for C's atomic store; no live dispatch before them |
| D16 | All 5 result exports | Stable replay/execution boundary; acknowledgement is not a deal or terminal proof |

This explains the DTO bottleneck honestly: EvidenceRecord pulls in all evidence payloads;
NegotiationState pulls in strategic history helpers; EventProposal pulls in all hydrated event
variants; ReplayResult pulls in closing types. **Do not narrow those unions or redefine public
ports to chase a smaller count.** Most savings come from earlier component work and deferred
algorithms, not from removing schema definitions. C's immutable field/invariant definitions
remain binding whenever a type is implemented.

## D. Early behavioral acceptance and honest gates

T6.1 local behavior work starts with T3.1, rather than after M5. Keep the present preference
flip, greeting, refusal, uncertainty, injection and economic-ceiling tests. Extend them with
small controlled scenario pairs; production inputs never contain desired actions or evaluation
labels. Replays of model drafts test grounding/plumbing, not independent language understanding.

| Requested behavior | Controlled local test / defensible acceptance |
|---|---|
| Legitimate cost pressure versus flexibility | Same buyer terms; vary reported pressure and separately corroborating applicable cost evidence. Supported pressure changes rationale/feasible exchange or clarification; flexibility supports an affordable price/term request. No invented discount, automatic concession or sustainable-margin hard floor |
| Payment constraint changes concession structure | New separately identified synthetic fixture with payment and another approved negotiable lever; compare reported payment refusal with flexibility. Prefer the admissible other lever when justified; recompute complete costs. P10 payment stays fixed at 30 days/DAP; no P10 golden mutation |
| Volume-dependent discount | Separate synthetic case with at least two volumes satisfying must-haves; preserve conditional supplier offer as reported evidence, evaluate its actual legal packages including uncovered need/commitment. Test a beneficial and a harmful trade. P10 only permits 23,400 after must-haves and cannot demonstrate a volume-choice flip |
| Irrelevant wording | Greeting/paraphrase preserves semantic strategy and package/economics. Raw input and record hashes may change; do not demand identical provenance IDs |
| Unsupported assertion | Claimed cost rise remains reported constraint/hypothesis with citations; unsupported or contradictory evidence cannot become canonical fact or outward verified claim. Missing/ambiguous approval yields unknown/clarify |
| Strategy cannot bypass checks | Favor an over-ceiling candidate, invent an ID/edit a package, or recommend illegal/private output. Real evaluator and independent validator reject; executor receives no rejected action. Trace the rejection and admitted fallback/cannot-decide |

Checkpoint B includes actual selected-action comparisons, not only intent-direction assertions.
An appropriately unchanged action with a changed explanation is allowed where economics/legal
constraints dominate; include controlled affordable scenarios where the action must change.
Compare source revision → assessment category/citations → intent → candidate/economic delta →
selection → validation in the trace. Test outcomes under a fixed clock/config; repeat locally
without hosted calls. Add manifest entries only for the focused tests introduced for each slice.

Keep three independent claims: **structural correctness** (schemas/ports/hashes), **behavioral
correctness** (controlled relevant and irrelevant differences), **negotiation performance**
(held-out independent outcomes, costs/regret/failures). A fake acknowledgement demonstrates
neither persuasion nor savings. Later T3.4/T6 evaluations measure held-out model precision,
grounding, unsupported assertions, latency and strategy outcomes under separately allowed usage.

No gate machinery rewrite is needed. The existing `--v2-dto-require` accepts symbols and batches;
`--v2-require` accepts selected module prefixes. Define each milestone's test selectors AND
required symbol list. Run all contract tests for implemented symbols, not just happy-path examples.
Missing required symbols/components fail; present malformed symbols, failed assertions and broken
imports never xfail. List later unimplemented tests explicitly. The final full-contract gate stays
`tests/v2 --v2-require all` (including optional/deferred exports); never use it to announce an
intermediate capability complete. Run appropriate full repository checks before a future push,
reporting inherited failures separately.

## E. Precise proposed document amendments

Apply these localized changes when adopting this proposal; they were **not applied in this pass**:

1. **D-roadmap.md §1:** replace “Freeze shared models first” with “Freeze each implemented
   boundary contract before its consumer; deliver dependency-complete DTO groups alongside
   vertical component increments.” Add A–E crosswalk above; retain original M rows and evidence.
   Change the diagram's whole-T1.1 arrows to consumed-contract prerequisites, not a new design.
2. **task-specs.md T1.1d and batch graph:** retain D inventories and graph; remove the mandatory
   global serial D1–D16 implementation barrier. Require topological symbol-level dependencies,
   complete unions, serial shared-file ownership and documented handoffs. Batch completion
   still requires every batch export. Change T1.2a/T1.4/T2.1/T4.1 dependencies to the exact
   consumed-type closure. Split T1.2a P10 bindings from advanced scenario bindings, T5.1 used
   offer/question validation from full claims/closing coverage, and T6.1 local controls from
   later complete performance evaluation. Retain full-parent acceptance; no completed labels.
3. **C-interfaces.md §8.5 only:** clarify that scenario-only RecordedInputs fields can remain
   unavailable until their consuming checkpoint, without inventing generic payloads, and that
   partial codec availability does not satisfy the full fixture contract. No port signature,
   DTO field, tagged union, or package migration change proposed.
4. **implementation-guide.md / test-catalog.md / E-evaluation.md:** add checkpoint-specific
   selector/symbol gate recipes and the six controlled scenarios above. Preserve all existing
   assertions and full-contract gate. Existing test runner already supports these narrower gates.
5. **Tracker and first-three-prompts.md:** link this addendum; show T1.1a–c and four metadata
   DTOs as implemented, remaining T1.1d as incremental/planned, and the next assignment below.
   Keep the original prompts as historical completed assignments, not the current queue.

No architecture rewrite, DTO deletion, V1 repair, golden change or research-platform task is
needed to adopt this execution order.

## F. Immediate next implementation assignment

**T2.1 first increment + consumed T1.1d symbols: typed layered evidence resolver.** This is a
bounded, demonstrable algorithm before the rest of the DTO inventory. It addresses the known
case-overlay correctness issue and feeds the evidence-conditioned decision path. It is not
the complete ContextBuilder or checkpoint A/B; those remain unfinished.

Copy-ready prompt (use after accepting the dependency-order amendment):

```text
Implement the first T2.1 evidence-resolution increment, with only its necessary
T1.1d contract closure. Read AGENTS.md, docs/README.md, docs/10-implementation-checklist.md,
docs/v2/C-interfaces.md §8.9 D1/D2, task-specs.md and this implementation-order addendum.
Preserve all pre-existing working-tree changes. Do not modify V1, frozen fixtures,
existing assertions, dependencies, CLI defaults, or use network/hosted/model calls.

Owned production files: extend src/negotiator/v2/core/models.py;
create src/negotiator/v2/evidence/__init__.py and evidence/resolver.py.
Implement exactly these 13 missing exports, preserving C's fields and validation:
IndexFact, ScorecardFact, CostFact, QuoteFact, ContractFact, ForecastFact,
OrderPriceFact, TextRecord, NamedEstimate, EstimateRecord, EvidencePayload,
EvidenceRecord, Conflict. Reuse the four existing metadata DTOs and foundation models.
Define the entire EvidencePayload tagged union; no dict/Any/model_construct escape.

Implement a pure typed LayeredEvidenceResolver internal service over
tuple[EvidenceRecord, ...]. Its resolve method returns immutable resolved records,
Conflict entries and Issue entries (a typed tuple return is sufficient; do not add
a new shared DTO). This helper is internal to evidence and will be injected/used
by the later LayeredContextBuilder; do not alter ContextBuilder's public Protocol.
Scope this first method to explicit base/release/case records; reject unsupported
layers with a typed issue rather than inventing their priority.

Resolve by canonical identity before applicability: case > release > base;
replace whole records, never fill removed fields from a lower layer. Distinct
records with equal highest priority for one canonical identity produce an
unresolved blocking Conflict and no usable winner. Collapse identical repeats
by record identity/content; contradictory reuse of an identity is an error.
Preserve statement/estimate/hypothesis kind; same identifier cannot promote an
unverified record into a canonical fact. Do not merge unrelated unkeyed statements.
Keep input records unchanged so the later prepared context can retain shadowed
revisions; conflict IDs reference those original records.
After selecting a version, check its explicit supplier/part/case scope against
supplied target identifiers. An inapplicable winner reports scope_mismatch and
must not revive the base record. Preserve supplied provenance, disclosure, basis
and temporal metadata verbatim; calendar/freshness derivation is a later context task.
No cost estimate, claim verification, interpretation or strategy in this resolver.

Add focused direct resolver tests in tests/v2/contracts/test_layered_resolver.py.
Construct validated EvidenceRecord inputs directly; no full codec prerequisite.
Test base/release/case replacement, null/deleted optional fields, equal-priority
collision, identical replay, conflicting record identity, scope-after-precedence,
unkeyed supplier statements, no authority promotion, exact basis/provenance,
and input immutability/deterministic output. Use real changed record values, not
fixture IDs that select expected winners. If the specification does not settle a
case, record a narrow issue rather than silently inventing a public invariant.

Acceptance: all existing remaining-DTO tests for those 13 symbols pass under
explicit --v2-dto-require requirements, including negative/exact-field/round-trip
and additional applicable cases; direct resolver tests pass with the new evidence
module required; foundation/boundary/hardening/evidence-metadata tests remain passing.
Ruff on src/negotiator/v2 and tests/v2 passes; frozen V1 replay stays exact.
Run the whole V2 suite and report remaining xfails without hiding failures.
For batch gates, D1 is complete; D2 remains partial. T2.1 and T1.1d remain in progress.

Deliver a small completion note: implemented symbols, selector/gate commands and
results, a concrete cost-record override example with winner/conflict provenance,
remaining gaps, and the next consumer (LayeredContextBuilder + typed recorded inputs).
No checkpoint A/B, full-contract, live-readiness or negotiation-performance claim.
```

This first task deliberately couples a small exact contract closure to an immediately useful
implementation. Follow it with consumer-sized case/economic DTOs and T4.1, then typed P10
bindings/composition; do not resume the remaining fifteen batches as an uninterrupted queue.

## G. First T2.1 increment: verified local implementation

**Source:** `a88bf86` plus preserved pre-existing working changes; no branch/commit/push,
V1 source edit, dependency change, or external call. Implemented the 13 exports in F exactly
against C and the existing DTO examples: D1 is complete; five D2 exports are complete;
D2, T1.1d and T2.1 remain in progress. The resolver is an internal evidence service returning
typed immutable records/conflicts/issues; no public Protocol or DTO-field revision was needed.

**Concrete result:** synthetic `cost:310010` resolves from base EUR 132.64 to release EUR 140.00
to case EUR 150.00, retaining the selected original record, source layer/hash/locator and a
nonblocking conflict referencing all shadowed revision IDs. Removing the case selects release;
an out-of-scope case selects neither release nor base and reports `scope_mismatch`. Equal-priority
distinct revisions have no winner. Contradictory record identities or unsupported session/derived
layers block the affected identity. Statements/hypotheses remain their supplied kind.

**Verification:** direct resolver/supplemental safety contracts **53 passed**; remaining-DTO
suite with D1 plus explicit NamedEstimate/EstimateRecord/EvidencePayload/EvidenceRecord/Conflict
requirements **263 passed, 600 explicit unimplemented xfails**; whole V2 suite with core,
config, evidence.resolver and those symbols required **509 passed, 720 explicit unimplemented
xfails**, zero unexpected failures. V2 source/tests Ruff, frozen V1 replay, and diff whitespace
checks pass. Expanded test manifest regenerated to 1,229 cases, retaining old assertions/goldens.
The legacy four-failure classification from section A remains; this increment does not repair V1.

Reproduce the full scoped gate:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v2 \
  --v2-require core --v2-require config --v2-require evidence.resolver \
  --v2-dto-require D1 --v2-dto-require NamedEstimate --v2-dto-require EstimateRecord \
  --v2-dto-require EvidencePayload --v2-dto-require EvidenceRecord --v2-dto-require Conflict
```

**Next increment: connect resolved evidence to its cost consumer.** Implement the existing
T2.3 `EvidenceProjections.cost_input(EvidenceContext, canonical_id) -> ResolvedCostInput`
contract with only EvidenceContext, RelevanceRecord and ResolvedCostInput added. Direct tests
compose this resolver's output into a validated EvidenceContext and call that consumer; full
ContextBuilder/preparation/codec are not prerequisites. Propagate blocking conflict, scope,
missing-source, kind, temporal uncertainty and basis issues instead of issuing a trusted cost
from a supplier assertion. If no admissible cost exists, fail explicitly through the existing
contract-error boundary; do not fabricate the required ResolvedCostInput.unit_cost or weaken
the return type. Preserve the exact winner SourceRefs and price basis and retain disclosure
on its source context;
EUR 150/140 source changes must reach cost input and invalidate its economic input fingerprint.
Keep internal_cost_claim and full T2.3 incomplete until their own contracts/services exist.

Then exercise T4.1 directly using its existing OfficialCostOracle/EconomicEvaluator boundaries
and validated case/economic inputs, while adding a small T4.3 policy comparison driven by those
actual results and cited supplier assessments. The OfficialCostOracle input/output closure
currently needs 16 missing exports, rather than the complete 147 remaining exports. This is
consumer contract work alongside real arithmetic, not a new batch-only queue. The first
behavioral demonstration should compare identical legal candidates under changed applicable
cost evidence/grounded supplier preference and show the affordable selected action plus the
source/assessment/economic explanation; include irrelevant wording and inadmissible advice
controls. Selection and used-action validation must remain independent. Full ContextBuilder
integration follows when its server/case contracts exist; persistence and the ten-stage loop
remain integration work. No intelligent negotiation or live-readiness claim is made yet.

## H. T2.3 cost consumer: verified local implementation

Implemented `EvidenceProjections.cost_input(context, canonical_id)` in evidence/claims.py;
added only RelevanceRecord, EvidenceContext and ResolvedCostInput from C §8.9 D2. The DTO
fields/defaults remain unchanged. Direct tests feed this consumer the working resolver's
selected records/conflicts/gaps through a validated EvidenceContext. No ContextBuilder,
prepared-data loader, persistence, orchestration, strategy, or official arithmetic was added.

**Demonstrated:** release EUR 140 becomes case EUR 150 under authoritative source precedence;
the projected Price and exact economic SourceRef revision change, as does
`semantic_hash(ResolvedCostInput)`. This is the fingerprint of this narrow typed economic input,
not the still-unimplemented complete EconomicContext fingerprint. Revision-only changes also
invalidate the input hash; unrelated supplier wording changes neither projection nor hash.
Declared EUR/price units (1/100/1000), part basis, scope and temporal attribution are preserved
without numerical conversion. Basis IDs remain distinct from evidence SourceRefs. Internal
disclosure remains on the original context/source, not a fabricated new DTO field.

**Failures are explicit ContractViolation exceptions:** missing/ambiguous cost, conflict with
the selected winner, supplier statements/estimates/hypotheses or text payloads, inadmissible
scope/layer, unknown/stale/future temporal status, contradictory explicit validity dates, and
ambiguous/wrong-part price basis. The consumer also fails closed on context error gaps because
the selected-only view may not identify the canonical source affected by a discarded revision;
warnings are retained. This is conservative and can block a cost when an unrelated error is
present. It does not silently fall back or claim that unrelated missing data has been resolved.
Source bytes, prep hashes and freshness-rule execution remain upstream preparation work; this
increment checks declared metadata and dates, and does not establish source authenticity itself.

**Checks:** direct projection acceptance **29 passed**; existing remaining-DTO suite with the
three new symbols required **275 passed, 588 explicit unimplemented xfails**; full V2 with
implemented core/config/evidence components and consumed symbols required **550 passed,
708 explicit unimplemented xfails**, zero unexpected failures. V2 Ruff, frozen V1 replay and
diff whitespace checks pass. Expanded test manifest regenerated to 1,258 cases; existing
assertions and golden fixtures preserved. T2.3 remains partial: internal_cost_claim, estimate
construction, full claim verification and the complete financial evaluation are unfinished.

**Smallest next task toward direct T4.1 evaluation:** implement
`adapters/official.py:OfficialArithmetic.evaluate(CaseContract, ResolvedTerms,
SupplierEstimate | None) -> OfficialCostResult` through the existing OfficialCostOracle port,
with its 16 missing input/output exports only. Pair those types with the actual pinned-kit
calculation in the same bounded increment; no DTO-only batch or complete factory prerequisite.
Use direct validated inputs and independent official component/cents parity tests, preserving
fixed terms, quote standards and price basis. A source-derived cost remains an attributed input
to explicit estimate construction; it must never overwrite BuyerEconomics or the official
cost function. With estimates disabled, changing evidence alone must not alter official costs.
With an explicit admitted supplier estimate, the official relationship calculation owns any
cost effect; retain the cost source revision in estimate assumptions. Do not use the legacy
inverse-pricing helper. OfficialArithmetic is an oracle adapter, not yet the complete
EconomicEvaluator or an action-selection/validation certificate. Follow with evaluated legal
candidate comparison and a small grounded T4.3 policy treatment for the first decision demo.


## I. T4.1 official arithmetic: verified local implementation

Implemented `adapters/official.py:OfficialArithmetic.evaluate` through the unchanged
OfficialCostOracle interface. Added only its 16 missing exports: all 13 D3 exports and
SupplierEstimate, CostComponent and OfficialCostResult. D3 is complete; D4 and T4.1 remain
partial. No EconomicEvaluator, strategy, inverse solver, orchestration or persistence was added.

The adapter calls the pinned arena kit's cost_breakdown and total_cost (lock revision
`1b5516bb95ef28e37f69aa446dc62168864bca53`). Decimal inputs convert explicitly at its float
boundary; components preserve kit values and totals preserve kit rounding. Tests verify installed
cost-source bytes against the pinned local source. No formulas or inverse helper are copied.
Evidence costs cannot overwrite buyer inputs; relationship effects require a separately
supplied validated SupplierEstimate.

**Exact parity:** all eleven components and totals match for three frozen P10 packages under

The code confirms that the offline pipeline currently has no language-driven commercial policy: the interpreter echoes messages, the proposer emits fixed intents, and the selector ranks supplied packages by cost.

+## 3. Architectural assessment
+
+The core separation is commercially useful: models can vary while arithmetic, evidence
+authority and execution admission remain constant. The risk is treating the pipeline's
+interfaces as an already capable negotiator, or forcing all future strategy into a weak
+single-dimension intent language.
+
+| Boundary | Assessment of responsibilities, coupling and LLM suitability | Recommendation |
+|---|---|---|
+| Preparation/resolution | Correct separation of precedence, scope and provenance; typed records avoid supplier-statement promotion. Preparation is still declared/synthetic | Preserve resolver; fix case-fact consumption; wrap pinned readers for the first real evidence types when needed |
+| Context assembly | Correct immutable snapshot seam; currently strict global gates, empty relevance and no documents. Private recorded DTO is a focused adapter, not full codec completion | Reuse for experiments; add a bounded relevance/disclosure projection rather than a retrieval platform |
+| Interpretation | Assessment collections are expressive for requests, refusals, conditions, roles/approval gaps and hypotheses; exact quotes are checked but entailment is not established | Existing port suffices now; implement semantic interpreter and independent labels |
+| Proposal | Async read-only seam is suitable. Single dimension/direction cannot explicitly express joint conditional trades, price search choices or priority | Small versioned intent/projection extension for milestone 2; no extra strategic service |
+| Generation | Right owner for legal numerical construction. Supplied package wrapper is a test implementation, not a commercially useful search method | Add bounded legal option/tick construction; retain incomplete-search diagnostics |
+| Economics | Right authority and reuse boundary; parity tested. Partial-sheet resolution is useful here but insufficient for outbound admission | Preserve oracle/evaluator; correct tick check; settle nominal convention only when multiple scenarios are enabled |
+| Selection | Correct approved-batch seam; permits strategic value beyond lowest immediate cost. Current minimum-cost test selector cannot express acceptance/round/information trade-offs | First LLM ranking experiment here; relative economic descriptions and grounded history |
+| Rendering | Fixed templates create a strong initial boundary. “Renderer must not call a model” is compatible with a future injected validated communication draft, but current render signature carries no such artifact | Keep templates now; later add a narrow communication-draft handoff, not model text hidden in rationale |
+| Validation | Correct independent economic/identity/byte boundary; independence means separate authority, not duplicate arithmetic formulas | Exact outgoing fields, declared ticks and future claim/commitment checks must be explicit |
+| Orchestration | Injected ports genuinely support substitution; eight-stage coordinator is enough for one offline decision. It cannot yet register research batches or execute hold/close outcomes | Extend locally for call ledger/fallback and requested capability; do not replace coordinator/framework |
+| Memory/store | Schemas describe sensible separation of server, strategy and operation truth. No working store means offline trace cannot grant dispatch authority | Use supplied history and prior assessments initially; durable state/operations for real multi-turn sending |
+| Model/provider | Single typed async gateway is appropriate; task/result unions, explicit config and usage preserve provider independence | Implement consumed closure; add propose only for its first consumer |
+
+### Proposal, generation and selection: who decides what?
+
+**The LLM chooses the commercial objective and trade hypothesis.** Examples: seek a price
+reduction in return for a legal delivery concession; test whether commitment matters; stop
+repeating a specifically refused exchange; ask who can approve a condition. It reads prior
+offers/concessions, source-backed observations, uncertainty and remaining rounds.
+
+**Code constructs exact numerical packages.** It takes allowed option IDs, an explicit
+anchor/reference and registered search instructions; creates complete sheets on legal ticks;
+and exposes the explored alternatives and rejected regions. Supplier-quoted numbers remain
+source-attributed observations until admitted through code. An LLM may request an aggressive
+price band or another legal option; it has no numeric execution authority. This follows the
+repository invariant that transmitted numbers and sheets come from code.
+
+**Economics evaluates every concrete package using the official model.** It does not invent
+supplier acceptance probabilities or turn a should-cost observation into a hard supplier floor.
+Generation can call the evaluator for bounded construction, while final evaluation/validation
+still certify the exact retained output.
+
+**Selection chooses the next concrete action, including a question.** It may prefer an
+affordable higher-cost package if grounded supplier information makes that exchange more
+credible, or spend a round clarifying a material ambiguity. It considers concession history,
+deadline/round opportunities and uncertainty. Its prediction of supplier reactions is a
+hypothesis, not official economic value.
+
+Keep the strategic/tactical distinction within these existing ports. A new “strategic planner”
+service is unnecessary. Short internal decision explanations should state the observed signal,
+chosen exchange and unknown that could invalidate it; they should not store private chain-of-thought.
+
+Do not compute expected negotiation value by assigning invented acceptance probabilities.
+When calibrated predictions eventually exist, compare expected terminal cost and no-deal
+consequences under explicit assumptions. Until then, use qualitative uncertainty and controlled
+outcome experiments. Preserve the difference between **buyer cost if accepted** and
+**likelihood/trajectory of acceptance**.
+
+Model choice of hold should produce an engine outcome with a bounded recheck, not a fake
+zero-cost question. A close request goes to a fresh deterministic closing evaluator. The
+model never sends accept/walk or establishes terminal truth.
+
+## 4. Recommended intelligence architecture
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    Raw["Immutable messages, standing sheets and acknowledged history"] --> I["Grounded supplier interpreter"]
+    E["Resolved evidence plus bounded relevance/disclosure projection"] --> I
+    E --> P["LLM strategic proposal policy"]
+    I --> A["Assessment: observations, reported constraints, hypotheses, unknowns"]
+    A --> P
+    H["Read-only attempts, concessions, conditions and question history"] --> I
+    H --> P
+    P --> G["Code: complete legal option and price-tick candidates"]
+    G --> O["Existing official economic evaluation"]
+    O --> S["Approved-ID strategic selection"]
+    A --> S
+    H --> S
+    S --> R["Templates first; later validated communication draft"]
+    E --> C["Canonical claim and disclosure verification"]
+    C --> R
+    R --> V["Independent final validation and exact bytes"]
+    V --> T["Offline trace and evaluation"]
+    V --> X["Later: atomic ownership, executor and recovery"]
+    X --> F["Observed feedback and authoritative state"]
+    F --> H
+    Q["Optional bounded hypothetical lookahead"] -.-> P
+    Q -.-> S
+```
+
+The interpreter, proposer and selector are logical components, not autonomous agents.
+One configured model can serve them through different purpose projections/prompts. Separate
+interfaces make failures and ablations interpretable without requiring separate providers.
+
+### First LLM decision: two calls, existing tasks
+
+Start with **interpret + select**, using the supplied-candidate generator as a temporary
+bounded candidate universe and a small registered question set. This isolates whether
+language understanding changes an affordable choice. The selector should choose between a
+genuinely supplier-relevant exchange and a cheaper but explicitly unsuitable alternative;
+it must not simply restate the cost minimum.
+
+The first selector receives code-authored descriptions of exact approved packages, relative
+cost deltas/scenario ordering, relevant attempts/refusals and the grounded assessment.
+`SelectionOption.summary` can support this bounded description today; do not encode an
+untyped protocol inside it. Cite the allowed sources. No absolute reservation, fallback
+values, private targets, full cost estimates, hidden score targets or evaluation labels enter
+the provider projection.
+
+Implement M's **15 missing gateway exports**, retaining all members of ModelInput and
+ModelResult, plus `SelectorResponse` for the second consumer. This is a dependency-complete
+consumer handoff, not a request to finish D12/D13 or all remaining contracts.
+
+An interpreter-only feature would measure understanding but leave the fixed proposal/minimum
+selector unable to use it. A selector-only direct LLM treatment is a useful cheaper comparison,
+but should not become the only evidence representation. Both treatments can share economics
+and validation.
+
+### Call scheduling for proposal intelligence
+
+C requires at most **two calls total**, 35 seconds compute, initial interpreter/selector caps
+of 8/4 seconds, and fallback/submission reserves. Fresh ModelBudget objects must not reset
+the per-decision ledger. A four-call interpreter→proposer→selector→writer design conflicts
+with this contract.
+
+For the next proposal treatment, use **interpret + propose**, with a mechanical selector
+that honors the model's validated strategic priority and uses economics to rank concrete
+variants within an admitted intent. Include a baseline intent and clarification fallback.
+This is a small selector rule, not an elaborate deterministic strategy. Keep the
+interpret+select arm as a common comparator.
+
+Later compare a fused assessment/proposal draft plus select if latency/quality justifies the
+additional adapter coupling. Any such combined task needs an explicit output contract and
+per-decision cache identity; do not invisibly reuse a select call for planning. Raising the
+two-call cap is an operational/contract decision justified by measured benefit and latency.
+
+### Interpretation, opponent model and memory
+
+Use existing assessment types:
+
+- Exact offers/requests/refusals/conditional statements become `GroundedObservation` with
+  original message spans and package references when identifiable.
+- Numerically explicit supplier constraints become `ReportedConstraint`, retaining
+  `authority="supplier_reported"`, condition references and active/stale/superseded status.
+- Soft preferences, willingness or tactical interpretations become `PreferenceHypothesis`
+  with support, contradiction and qualitative confidence. Do not create numeric willingness
+  from tone or unverified prose.
+- Ambiguous scope, approval, contradiction and missing support become uncertainties/unknowns
+  and a registered clarification opportunity.
+
+Observed constraints need not be legal option values: a supplier's illegal 54-day statement
+is still evidence of what it said. Outgoing construction remains restricted to allowed options.
+Approval language does not establish actual authority or a standing acceptable sheet.
+Conditional offers must retain all conditions; a cited clause taken out of its antecedent is
+not grounded agreement.
+
+The first useful opponent model is this **qualitative, cited assessment over history**.
+It can distinguish changed positions and hypotheses without a second belief engine.
+Role changes weaken earlier authority/preference assumptions. Probabilistic utility models,
+cross-session learning and specialized imitation are research experiments.
+
+First memory needs raw chronological messages/standing sheets, acknowledged buyer packages,
+their actual changes, scoped refusals/conditions, questions and known answers, latest validated
+assessment plus parent references, and consumed claim/operation status when those features
+exist. Keep proposals separate from sent actions. Supplied immutable history is enough for
+offline multi-turn experiments; do not require a database to test it.
+
+Namespaced `StrategyMemory` can later hold a strict compact hypothesis/plan artifact. Its
+schema must be owned and versioned, but no generic memory subsystem or embedding store is
+needed. Do not let a summary erase contradictory raw messages.
+
+### Evidence as a commercial capability
+
+There are two distinct evidence effects:
+
+| Effect | Example | Authority |
+|---|---|---|
+| Changes official evaluated economics | Admitted cost plus explicit full-cost/rate assumptions changes the official relationship penalty | Existing projection/estimate/oracle path; buyer economics unchanged |
+| Changes strategic reasoning or argument | Recent delivery evidence supports a schedule question; a contract notice supports a timing challenge; opposing index evidence weakens a cost-rise story | Cited observations/hypotheses and separately verified outward claims; no automatic cost/price change |
+
+The current demonstration proves only the first effect. Build the second through a small
+evidence packet: supplier/part/case applicability, recent offer and quote standards, a handful
+of relevant drivers/contracts/performance observations, a retained contradiction, explicit
+gaps and disclosure status. Use the existing indexes and deterministic topic/date/scope
+selection before considering semantic retrieval.
+
+Relevance is a ranking, not truth. Never remove the only adverse or contradictory record
+because it weakens the buyer's argument. Distinguish declared current status from actually
+executed freshness rules and authenticated bytes. Missing proof stays unknown. Keep evidence
+and estimates independently source-linked.
+
+For an external model, filter entire unsafe records/snippets and previous assessment content,
+including numeric effects and copied raw text. A field allowlist alone cannot remove private
+values embedded in prose. Do not rewrite an EvidenceRecord's payload under its original
+identity and call that authentic redaction. Use approved snippets with original lineage or
+exclude the record until a proper projection exists.
+
+Each proposed move should identify the source-backed opportunity, what it does and does not
+establish, and the disclosable argument if any. A supplier assertion may justify asking for
+support even when it cannot become a canonical cost or outward claim.
+
+### Grounded communication
+
+Keep exact no-claim templates for the first intelligence milestone. Then expand to richer
+registered questions and conditional-exchange explanations whose terms are inserted by code.
+This yields useful persuasive communication earlier than unrestricted writing.
+
+For later model wording, provide only a selected action, approved claim sentences/IDs,
+permitted public snippets, tone and registered communicative objective. Return a strict
+communication draft with claim/span lineage and no commercial-action fields. A composition
+adapter injects the drafted artifact into a renderer; the renderer does not call a provider.
+
+The renderer binds exact selected terms and canonical claims. The independent validator
+checks the final body, numerical assertions, confidentiality, conditional commitments,
+recipient, claim usage/limits, package identity and exact bytes. Numbers in prose are checked
+against approved terms/claims; IDs cannot be stripped to leave an unsupported assertion.
+Nonnumeric promises also need an allowed commitment vocabulary. Supplier/model instruction
+attempts cannot add commitments or tools.
+
+There is no universal deterministic proof of arbitrary natural-language entailment. Start
+with canonical factual/commitment clauses and bounded connective wording. Any supplemental
+model judge is an evaluated aid, not an authority that makes free prose safe. On failure,
+render the already approved template; never let a writer revise the commercial decision.

Do not imitate deceptive urgency or private-data exposure | Same strategy ports; cross-opponent tests and equal-budget controls before claiming generalization |
+| R1, first optional experiment | [MERIT, ACL 2026](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.1155/) studies utility feedback, preference alignment and opponent awareness across AgoraBench settings, including prompting and training. Utility structure and human-preference assumptions differ from official procurement costs | Low/moderate: code-derived relative cost/trade descriptors plus short observed-outcome reflection. No fine-tuning initially; fabricated supplier utility or hidden-score leakage is a failure | Selector/proposal prompt treatment with/without feedback; same candidates, economics, provider and token budget |
+| R2, after useful generation | Leonardelli et al., [MESOs, 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S074959781630557X), reports six human experiments with first-offer choice and economic/relational benefits. Human findings do not predict supplier-bot response or later-turn effects | Moderate: 2–3 complete packages with approximately equivalent buyer cost and different permitted levers. Avoid claiming equal supplier value; diverse options may waste leverage or reveal flexibility | Generator + selector bundle; single-package versus small choice set, same admission/total budget, measure selected sheet and outcomes |
+| R3, cheap qualitative opponent model | Baarslag et al., [opponent-modeling survey, 2016](https://homepages.cwi.nl/~baarslag/pub/Learning_about_the_opponent_in_automated_bilateral_negotiation-a_comprehensive_survey_of_opponent_modeling_techniques.pdf), organizes modeling methods and evaluation. Many utility/domain assumptions require repeated informative observations | Low initially: cite stable preferences/refusals and isolate observed one-field deltas. Multi-field changes do not identify issue weights; role changes can invalidate inferred preferences | Assessment/memory; compare with no explicit model on held-out future quotes and actual decisions |
+| R4, label and information-gathering experiments | [CaSiNo, NAACL 2021](https://aclanthology.org/2021.naacl-main.254/) provides human campsite multi-issue dialogues and annotated persuasion strategies; associations are not procurement causal effects | Low/moderate: borrow annotation ideas, add approval/conditional/refusal labels and procurement questions. More labels are useful only if decisions improve; unnecessary questions consume scarce rounds | Interpreter/proposal; label ablation and ask-versus-offer against answer/refuse/no-answer counterparts, accounting for round cost |
+| R5, later bounded lookahead | Lewis et al., [Deal or No Deal?, EMNLP 2017](https://aclanthology.org/D17-1259/), demonstrates dialogue rollouts in hidden-utility item bargaining. Small trained bargaining models and known rewards differ from an uncertain supplier simulator | Moderate/high: one-step hypothetical responses for at most a few approved candidates. Hallucinated acceptance, role drift and model self-confirmation are principal risks | Optional simulation/research seam; equal-compute direct-selection baseline, held-out response prediction and deadline stress |
+| R6, only with suitable repeated interactions | Liu et al., [opponent simulation, ICML 2026](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/liu26ef.html), combines in-context imitation and best-of-N response search in repeated negotiation games. A short one-off procurement thread may lack the required data | High relative to present needs: reusable bounded opponent hypothesis and simulation, never canonical server evidence. Beware nonstationarity, sparse history and extra calls | Namespaced memory/proposal/selector; adaptation-vs-reset and equal-inference-cost comparisons before any runtime integration |
+
+Use [Faratin, Sierra and Jennings, 1998](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/252117/) for simple
+time/behavior concession controls, not as a requirement to build a sophisticated deterministic
+policy. Its formal service-negotiation model supplies algorithmic baselines, not empirical
+procurement guarantees.
+
+The immediate research investment is the comparison design and small feedback/qualitative-model
+ablations. Defer generic game-theoretic utility estimation, extensive self-reflection, deep
+rollouts, best-of-N imitation, training and cross-account models until a simple LLM treatment
+has a measured gap. Questions can enter before lookahead: no calibrated value-of-information
+solver is required to compare asking against offering.

+## 7. Updated development roadmap

+### Success measures and minimal evaluation
+
+| Objective | Measure and initial gate | What the evidence can establish |
+|---|---|---|
+| Structural correctness | Required consumed contract/module gates, official cents/components, identity consistency; R1–R3 negatives; zero admitted hard-invalid outputs in bounded tests | Correct implemented scope, not language understanding |
+| Evidence-grounded reasoning | Valid source/span rate, supported/contradicted/missing distinctions, retained adverse evidence, disclosable-claim checks | Attribution and measured semantic support on reviewed corpus |
+| Supplier understanding | Precision/recall for constraint/refusal/condition/approval/preference categories; false-approval and invented-numeric rates; unknown/fallback rate | Held-out component understanding for stated corpus/model/prompt |
+| Strategic decision quality | Controlled affordable action differences, no needless repeat after scoped refusal, useful clarification, economy-aware concessions; expert admissible-set review | Appropriate decisions under fixed inputs; no supplier counterfactual outcome |
+| Negotiation performance | Complete terminal buyer cost, official score where available, agreement/no-deal, meaningful baseline savings/regret, rounds, timeouts, tokens/calls/spend, per-scope downside | Results against specified reactive counterparts; live transfer only from funded original live runs |
+| Execution reliability | Zero duplicate conflicting operations, invalid sends or fabricated terminal events; bounded recovery and exact ID/bytes across crashes | Operational capability of exercised runtime, not persuasion |

+Use a modest independently reviewed pilot, proposed initially as **24 controlled scenario pairs**
+covering delivery/commitment preferences, payment trade-offs in a separate legal synthetic case,
+conditional offers, scoped refusals, approval ambiguity, conflicting/unsupported evidence,
+and irrelevant/injected text. These are new proposed fixtures, not already available labels.
+Keep P10's actual fixed payment, options and compliant volume unchanged. Include a supplier
+preference comparison where economics stays fixed and a cost-only comparison where language
+stays fixed.
+
+Freeze held-out scenario/phrase groups before prompt tuning; independent labels remain outside
+production requests. Reviewers label spans, conditions/authority and admissible action sets,
+not one demanded response string. Include controlled cases in which a more expensive affordable
+package is defensible, and cases where ceilings correctly dominate language. A greeting should
+preserve commercial behavior even if provenance/trace hashes change.
+
+Proposed semantic gate: zero false critical numeric/approval assertions in the safety subset;
+report category precision/recall and abstention, with quantitative thresholds pre-registered
+after label review and before candidate scoring. A finite zero-failure sample is not a universal
+guarantee. Fake/recorded drafts establish plumbing and adversarial controls; only separately
+authorized real model runs establish that the configured model understands unseen text.

+Compare four arms using the same inputs, candidate/economic/validation services:
+
+1. Supplied minimum-cost test strategy.
+2. Direct basic LLM selector using source-grounded observations/raw permitted input.
+3. Grounded LLM interpretation plus selector.
+4. One later feedback/opponent-model/proposal treatment.

+Use the same candidate universe when isolating selection. When evaluating generation, allow
+the treatment to produce new packages but include a common-universe comparison to distinguish
+search coverage from decision skill. Record provider/protocol/prompt/schema/model, source and
+case hashes, clock/config, cache information, raw permitted outputs, usage and fallbacks.
+Use equal call/token/time ceilings; report actual consumption.
+
+Add reactive multi-turn counterpart tests before performance claims: suppliers must respond to
+the actual proposed terms/questions. Historical fixed replies cannot measure the consequences
+of a different offer. Use several controlled counterpart policies with withheld thresholds/
+preferences, including conditional acceptance, information refusal and role changes; do not
+expose these internals in prompts. Calculate costs independently through the pinned kit.
+Report outcomes including failures and no-deal consequences; do not average only agreements.

+Interleave funded baseline/treatment sessions where permitted, retain the complete planned
+denominator and original failures, and report paired differences/uncertainty by independent
+scenario/supplier unit. Paraphrases, cache-identical runs and shared trajectories are not

+### Milestone 1 — Grounded intelligent offline decision
+
+**Objective/new capability:** supplier language and supported uncertainty change a commercially
+defensible next action under fixed legal/economic conditions.
+
+**Deliverables/modules:** R1–R3 fixes in evidence/context, economics/official and
+execution/validation; consumed model envelopes in core; adapters/model; intelligence/interpreter
+and fallback; bounded strategy selector; decision budget ledger in orchestration/budgets;
+minimal explicit composition and trace attribution. New focused labels/evaluator tool.
+
+**Dependencies/order:** bounded fixes and labels can begin immediately; define consumed contracts
+serially → fake gateway/call ledger → grounded interpreter → model selector → existing full
+offline coordinator. A fixed supplied-intent/generator baseline is acceptable only as the
+temporary candidate universe, clearly labelled.
+
+**Acceptance/tests:** require existing/new consumed DTO negatives and model timeout/cancellation/
+late-result/refusal/malformed/private-input controls; independent spans, conditions and revision
+checks; affordable action flips with unchanged economics; refusal/approval questions; irrelevant
+controls; actual official recomputation and final validation. Funded held-out model evaluation
+must accompany any claim of genuine LLM capability. Fake drafts alone earn plumbing status.
+
+**Exclusions:** new arbitrary offers, free prose/claims, research simulation, persistence or
+actual sending. **Risks:** semantic hallucination, candidate-set bias, insufficient 8/4-second
+provider latency, exact-quote checks mistaken for meaning. **Effort:** roughly 3–5 engineer-days,
+including fixtures/review, assuming a compatible approved provider and existing environment.
+Prototype coding can be faster; validation time still matters.
+
+### Milestone 2 — LLM-directed meaningful proposal generation
+
+**Objective/new capability:** construct new conditional price/term packages from actual case
+domains/history, rather than select only prewritten packages.
+
+**Deliverables/modules:** approved versioned ProposeInput/task/draft and joint intent directives;
+LLM strategy proposal implementation; economics/candidates and prices; small registered question
+catalog; updated batch-bound renderer/validator coverage where needed. Extend coordinator only
+for capability/budget handling.
+
+**Dependencies/order:** settle revision → implement exact contracts/adapter projection → legal
+option/tick construction → interpreter+proposer bundle with mechanical priority/cost selection
+→ compare to milestone-1 selector arm. Keep at most two calls. Generate at least one package
+fingerprint absent from the initial supplied list.
+
+**Acceptance/tests:** unseen legal synthetic multi-issue cases; all transmitted fields, bounds,
+ticks, must-haves and independent complete costs; conditional volume beneficial/harmful
+controls, price-specific versus broad refusal, no claim of supplier acceptance; bounded search
+exhaustion explicitly recorded. Same evidence revision can change strategic trade while disabled
+estimates leave arithmetic unchanged. Impossible needs produce clarification/cannot-decide.
+
+**Exclusions:** global optimum/inverse guarantee, calibrated utility or acceptance prediction,
+new term domains, live closing. **Risks:** strategic wishes yield no affordable package;
+missed combinations; refusal mis-scoping; high-dimensional search. **Effort:** 3–6 engineer-days,
+with one bounded case capability before generalization.
+
+### Milestone 3 — Evidence-grounded communication
+
+**Objective/new capability:** state a credible conditional exchange or verified commercial
+argument, preserving source/disclosure restrictions.
+
+**Deliverables/modules:** relevant T2.3 canonical claim oracle/verifier and T5.1 claim subset;
+registered question/exchange templates; permitted snippets; optional communication-draft adapter
+and handoff; execution/render and validation. Use existing claim-limit and disclosure contracts
+only when their first consumer is implemented.
+
+**Dependencies/order:** select one argument family → pinned-source verification/disclosure →
+canonical sentences/template composition → independent final-body checks → optional wording
+experiment under the unchanged call ceiling (reuse/precompute draft capability or keep templates;
+do not add an unbudgeted writer call).
+
+**Acceptance/tests:** wrong figures/IDs, stale/irrelevant/conflicting sources, duplicate usage,
+rival-recipient exception, private snippets, invented commitments, altered package values and
+prompt injection all blocked; fallback produces the approved template. Blind review of clarity/
+credibility plus communication ablation against reactive counterparts.
+
+**Exclusions:** arbitrary attachment exports, unrestricted persuasive prose, broad documents or
+guaranteed causal persuasion. **Risks:** verified-but-irrelevant argument, sensitive paraphrase,
+claim/commitment added by connective prose. **Effort:** 2–4 days for a bounded catalog/claim family;
+another 2–4 if model wording is justified.
+
+### Milestone 4 — Strategy experimentation and measured selection
+
+**Objective/new capability:** distinguish improvements in understanding, strategic decision
+quality and supplier outcomes under comparable conditions.
+
+**Deliverables/modules:** extend the small evaluator and manifests begun in milestone 1; vetted

+report effect sizes and uncertainty. Funded live trials need separate manifests and authorization.

+**Exclusions:** automatic promotion/default changes, large research portfolio, training, second
+dashboard. **Risks:** simulator-specific tactics, tuned labels, incomparable candidate sets,
+dependent repeats. **Effort:** 1–3 days of shared tooling plus 1–3 per small treatment, with
+evaluation/review/provider time additional.

+### Milestone 5 — Reliable multi-turn negotiation
+
+**Objective/new capability:** adapt to the actual consequences of sent actions across rounds,
+then preserve that behavior through crash/restart.
+
+**Deliverables/modules:** first an offline reactive supplier harness using immutable acknowledged
+history and official costs; then pure state/feedback projection, SQLite artifacts/state/outbox,
+closing evaluator/validation, allowed Arena adapter, executor/recovery and serial lifecycle.
+Reuse trace identities and low-level transport/readers; avoid copying mutable V1 decisions.
+
+**Dependencies/order:** implement reactive harness early alongside milestone 2; carry actual
+acknowledged history into interpretation/proposal; complete used-scope validation/closing →
+atomic state/operation storage → gateway/executor/recovery → integrated fault/restart suite.
+Basic feedback records linkage, not learned causal attribution.
+
+**Acceptance/tests:** supplier conditions/refusals/answers change subsequent actions; no phantom
+concessions from unsent drafts; same committed history survives restart; crash before/after
+commit/send/ack, uncertain open, reply loss, stale accept and missing terminal proof preserve
+original IDs/bytes or recovery-required status. All close triggers use fresh standing sheets
+and the same complete-cost comparison. No guaranteed agreement requirement for every fault.
+
+**Exclusions:** concurrent RFQ/wave optimization, cross-session learning, automatic causal
+credit assignment. **Risks:** inadequate remote proof, source/order ambiguity and late provider/
+transport results. **Effort:** 1–2 days for the initial reactive harness; roughly 5–9 additional
+days for durable serial execution/recovery and meaningful fault coverage.

+### Milestone 6 — Scope-specific competition readiness
+
+**Objective/new capability:** an authorized, operationally rehearsed agent whose selected scope
+has performance evidence and truthful failure/recovery behavior.
+
+**Deliverables/modules:** actual data/release-byte preparation and supported document standards;
+tested freshness/applicability; exact provider/protocol budget reports; intended CLI/Lab config/
+checkpoint parity; key/session/quota/endpoint restrictions; launch preflight and recovery/
+rollback runbook; funded original performance report. Resolve relevant inherited release
+failures and tooling gaps separately.
+
+**Dependencies/order:** stable intended intelligence scope and milestone-5 reliability → real
+input/provider protocol tests → exact launch rehearsal → explicitly allowed original baseline/
+candidate trials → scope-specific promotion decision before applicable freeze.
+
+**Acceptance/tests:** no forbidden spectator access, no hard-invalid sends or conflicting
+operation, authoritative terminal/round/deadline proof, official economic parity on actual
+bases, repeatable prepared inputs, measured budgets/fallback/timing, complete original outcome
+denominators and held-out scope. Test RFQ/all-thread closing if that is the release scope;

+
+**Exclusions:** automatic broad release from P10 alone, hidden-case optimum claims, post-freeze

+Effort ranges are engineering estimates, not measured completion times or an event-day promise.
+The sequence should stop or change if an intelligence treatment fails to improve decisions/

+### Reliability cutline
+
+Offline model experiments need strict filtered inputs, grounding checks, official economics,
+R1–R3 fixes, shared call/token/time limits, cancellation/late-result rejection, deterministic
+validated fallback and immutable snapshot consistency. Locally supplied synthetic evidence
+must be labelled; declared metadata does not become authenticated by hashing itself.
+
+Before consuming real files/providers, verify the exact bytes/config used and execute applicable
+freshness/disclosure rules. Before real sending, add durable operation ownership/CAS, atomic
+claim reservation when used, authoritative gateway parsing, retry/recovery, fresh standing-sheet
+closing, terminal verification and launch/quota/lease gates. A database and transport are not
+prerequisites to testing an interpreter on safe recorded inputs.
+
+Reuse pinned arithmetic/readers, claim formula/disclosure patterns, adviser ID/quote concepts,
+Lab records and low-level HTTP/idempotency patterns. Do not reuse the inverse helper, adviser
+daemon-thread waiter, mutable proposal-side memory, base-only dossier cost join or complete V1
+runner as trusted V2 components. Historical first-message parity remains a baseline obligation.

+| Decision | Recommended choice and rationale |

+| Delivery horizon | Treat V2 as an offline intelligence/continuing-development path unless all live gates fit before today's declared freeze. Avoid promising the multi-day roadmap for the current final |
